detail: finding: Albania is improving on transparency and aims to be fully digital but struggles to put citizens at the centre.
finding: Access to services and procedural information has improved; guidance, fees and contacts are online for almost every sampled service.
finding: Stakeholders say co-creation workshops are rare and working groups rely on experts, not end-user testing.
finding: The once-only principle shows a gap between law and practice.
metric: The monitor scores implementation of the once-only principle by providers at 3 of 3.
metric: The monitor scores citizens' reported experience of the once-only principle at 0.5 of 2.
intervention: The Code of Administrative Procedures institutionalises the one-stop-shop model under Article 74.
finding: No regulations clearly set requirements for citizen-centric service design.
finding: e-Albania has user analytics and star ratings, but detailed participation metrics are not systematically published.
finding: For most sampled services feedback exists and interoperability is used, fulfilling the once-only requirement.
intervention: VAT services run on their own e-Filing portal from the General Tax Directorate.
finding: Half of surveyed citizens agree they were not asked for documents the state holds, indicating partial implementation.
metric: Survey answers on not being asked for documents held by the state: 56.9% agree, 34.3% disagree.
finding: Albania has a solid foundation for citizen-centric delivery but significant challenges remain.
recommendation: Priorities are binding rules on citizen co-design and systematic publication of feedback and participation metrics.
finding: Modest improvements in service information through centralising details on e-Albania.
finding: Legal obligations on accessibility are clearer but practice stays fragmented and partial.
intervention: The Digital Agenda provides for mobile-friendly access through the e-Albania portal and app, and service passports.
finding: Central responsibility and user-oriented platforms significantly enhance efficiency and accessibility.
metric: The monitor scores the central platform as established and user-oriented at 4 of 4.
intervention: The e-Albania portal has an AI-based chatbot in Albanian and English.
finding: Feedback channels are in e-Albania, but key services outside the portal, such as vehicle registration and VAT, lack them.
outcome: Abolishing ADISA and moving its responsibilities to NAIS resolved institutional overlaps.
recommendation: MPAC and NAIS should issue a national methodology requiring co-creation and testing of services with end-users.
